title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
blurb: Stephen Covey argues that lasting success comes from character, not quick techniques or a polished image. He calls this working from the inside out: change how you see the world, and your behavior and results follow. The book lays out seven habits that move a person from dependence to independence, and then to interdependence. The first three habits build self-mastery: taking responsibility for your choices, defining what matters most, and organizing your time around it. The next three build strong relationships: seeking solutions where everyone wins, listening deeply before speaking, and creating results together that no one could reach alone. The seventh habit, sharpening the saw, keeps the whole system running through regular renewal of body, mind, heart and spirit. The result is a principle-centered way to live that grows stronger the more you practice it.

lessons.t: Change the Lens, Change the Life
lessons.b: How we see the world shapes everything we do, so lasting change starts with our paradigms and character, not surface techniques.
Between what happens to you and how you react lies a choice, and effective people focus their energy on what they can influence.

lessons.t: Begin With the End in Mind
lessons.b: Picture how you want to be remembered, then write a personal mission statement that guides your daily choices.
Spend more time on things that are important but not urgent, like planning, relationships and prevention, before they become crises.
Lasting relationships rest on deposits of trust and a mindset that seeks agreements where both sides genuinely benefit.
